config.title: Test Error Boundary

intro.title: Test Error Boundary
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a Vue component that catches and handles JavaScript errors in its child components, preventing the entire application from crashing. You'll learn about error boundaries, which are special components that wrap around other components to isolate failures. The main technologies involved are Vue's lifecycle hooks and error handling mechanisms. You'll implement this using Vue's errorCaptured hook and conditional rendering techniques. This is a fundamental pattern for building robust, production-ready Vue applications that gracefully handle unexpected errors.
intro.usecase: Error boundaries are essential in production Vue applications where components can fail unpredictably. In e-commerce dashboards, a faulty product recommendation widget shouldn't crash the entire shopping cart or checkout flow. Financial applications use error boundaries to isolate failing stock charts or data tables while keeping the main portfolio overview functional. This pattern allows developers to gracefully degrade specific UI sections - like a broken analytics panel in a SaaS dashboard - while maintaining core functionality and displaying user-friendly fallback messages.

objectives: Implement a Vue component that catches and handles errors from its child components
Configure error boundaries to display fallback UI when errors occur
Apply error boundary patterns to isolate component failures
Construct test cases that trigger errors within error boundary components
Initialize error state management within Vue's reactivity system
Render fallback content while preserving the main application functionality
Integrate error boundaries into existing Vue component hierarchies

steps.title: Import Vue and defineErrorHandler
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the defineErrorHandler function from the Vue package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and defineErrorHandler from 'vue'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing multiple items from a package
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue framework and defineErrorHandler function are imported and available for use.
successCriteria: Vue and defineErrorHandler are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both Vue and defineErrorHandler from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: import both Vue and defineErrorHandler from the Vue package.

steps.title: Create main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create and export a default Vue component named 'ErrorBoundaryTest' that returns a template with a single root <div> element.
steps.hint: Use the defineComponent function to create a Vue component. Remember to export it as default.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named 'ErrorBoundaryTest' is created and exported as the default export.
successCriteria: The component is defined with defineComponent, has the name 'ErrorBoundaryTest', and returns a template with a single root <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've used defineComponent, named it 'ErrorBoundaryTest', and included a template with a single root <div> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you're using defineComponent, naming it 'ErrorBoundaryTest', and returning a template with a single root element.

steps.title: Initialize error state
steps.instruction: Inside your component, use Vue's ref function to create a reactive state variable named 'error' initialized to null.
steps.hint: You'll need to import ref from 'vue' and call it with an initial value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a reactive error state variable ready to track error information.
successCriteria: The component contains a reactive state variable 'error' created with ref and initialized to null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using ref from 'vue' and initializing it to null.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a reactive state variable named 'error' using Vue's ref function.

steps.title: Create error throwing component
steps.instruction: Inside the ErrorBoundaryTest component's setup function, create a new child component called ErrorThrower that conditionally throws an error.
steps.hint: Define a component using defineComponent that has a prop or condition to trigger an error.
steps.expectedOutcome: A child component named ErrorThrower is defined inside the ErrorBoundaryTest component's setup function, ready to throw errors conditionally.
successCriteria: ErrorThrower component is defined with a condition that can throw an error.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a component, but make sure it's named ErrorThrower and has a condition that can throw an error.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ErrorThrower component is not properly defined. It should be created inside the setup function and have error-throwing logic.

steps.title: Define error handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named handleError that takes an error parameter and updates the error state with that error.
steps.hint: Create a function that will be called when an error occurs in child components. It should set the error state to the error parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named handleError is defined that will capture errors and update the error state.
successCriteria: The handleError function is defined inside setup, takes an error parameter, and updates the error state with that error.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your handleError function takes an error parameter and updates the error state with it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error handler function isn't defined correctly. Create a function named handleError that takes an error parameter and updates the error state.

steps.title: Register error handler with Vue
steps.instruction: In the setup function, call Vue's defineErrorHandler function to register your error handler function.
steps.hint: You need to call defineErrorHandler and pass your error handler function as an argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: The error handler function is properly registered with Vue's error handling system.
successCriteria: defineErrorHandler is called with the error handler function as its argument.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling defineErrorHandler and passing your error handler function to it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error handler isn't properly registered. You need to call defineErrorHandler with your error handler function.

steps.title: Add template structure
steps.instruction: Add a template section with a container div to your component.
steps.hint: In Vue single-file components, the template section defines the HTML structure. Add a <template> tag with a <div> inside.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: basic template structure
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a template section with a container div, ready for content.
successCriteria: A <template> tag with a <div> inside is added to the component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added both the <template> tag and a <div> element inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure isn't correct. Add a <template> section with a <div> inside to create the container.

steps.title: Add error display section
steps.instruction: Inside the template section, add a <div> that conditionally renders when an error has occurred. Display the error message using Vue's template syntax.
steps.hint: Use v-if to conditionally render the error display section based on whether error state exists. Inside the div, you can output the error message.
steps.analogousExample: // Conditional rendering in Vue template
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will include a conditional error display section that shows when an error occurs.
successCriteria: Template contains a div with v-if directive that conditionally renders based on error state, and displays the error message using template syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include both the v-if directive for conditional rendering and the template syntax to display the error message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet have the conditional error display section. Add a div with v-if that shows when there's an error, and display the error message inside it.

steps.title: Add error throwing component to template
steps.instruction: Inside the template's <div>, add the ErrorThrower component so it will be rendered.
steps.hint: In Vue templates, you can use a component by its name as a custom element tag.
steps.analogousExample: // Adding a component to a template
steps.expectedOutcome: The ErrorThrower component is included in the template, making it part of the rendered UI.
successCriteria: The template contains <ErrorThrower /> inside the <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the ErrorThrower component inside the <div> in the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ErrorThrower component is not yet added to the template. Add it inside the <div>.

steps.title: Add error trigger button
steps.instruction: Inside the ErrorThrower component's template, add a button element with the text 'Throw Error' that triggers the error-throwing behavior when clicked.
steps.hint: You'll need to add a button with a click handler that calls the function that throws an error.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button to trigger an action
<button @click="triggerError">Throw Error</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The ErrorThrower component will have a button that users can click to trigger an error.
successCriteria: A button element with the text 'Throw Error' is added to the ErrorThrower component's template with a click handler that triggers the error-throwing behavior.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it has the correct text and click handler to trigger the error-throwing behavior.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't properly configured to trigger errors. Check that you've added it to the ErrorThrower component with the correct click handler.

steps.title: Add error reset button
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a button element with the text 'Reset Error' that calls a resetError function when clicked.
steps.hint: You'll need to add the button in the template section and ensure it has a click handler that calls a function to reset the error state.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: button with click handler
<button @click="resetError">Reset Error</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Reset Error' appears in the template, ready to be wired to a reset function.
successCriteria: The template contains a <button> element with the text 'Reset Error' and an @click handler that calls resetError.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the correct text and click handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or incorrect. Add a <button> with text 'Reset Error' and @click="resetError".

steps.title: Add styling for error display
steps.instruction: Add CSS styles to make the error message visually distinct by adding a style section with error-specific styling.
steps.hint: Add a <style> section after the template and define CSS rules for the error display elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a style section with CSS rules that make error messages visually distinct.
successCriteria: A <style> section is added with CSS rules targeting error display elements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a style section, but make sure it includes specific CSS rules for error display elements.
steps.feedbackWrong: The style section is missing or incomplete. Add a <style> section with CSS rules for error messages.
